note: Community question bank for AWS Study Hub. Each question: id, cert, domain, question, options[], answer (index), explanation. Contributions welcome via PR.

questions.question: A company needs to run a workload that can be interrupted and restarted without data loss, and it must complete within 24 hours. Which EC2 pricing option provides the MOST cost savings?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% off On-Demand. Because the workload tolerates interruption and has a flexible 24-hour window, Spot is ideal. Reserved requires a 1-3 year commitment, and Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive.

questions.question: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which task is the CUSTOMER's responsibility when using Amazon RDS?
options: Configuring security groups and network access
questions.explanation: For managed services like RDS, AWS handles OS/engine patching and hardware. The customer configures security groups, NACLs, IAM, encryption settings, backups, and owns the data.

questions.question: Which AWS pricing model lets you commit to a consistent amount of compute usage (measured in $/hour) for a 1- or 3-year term in exchange for lower prices?
questions.explanation: Savings Plans give discounted rates in return for a committed spend ($/hour) over 1 or 3 years, and are more flexible than standard Reserved Instances.

questions.question: A startup wants to avoid large upfront hardware purchases and pay only for the compute it uses. Which cloud benefit does this describe?
options: Trading capital expense for variable expense
questions.explanation: Paying only for what you consume, instead of buying hardware upfront, is the classic 'trade capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense (OpEx)' benefit of cloud computing.

questions.question: A web application has high read traffic on its MySQL database. The team wants to improve read performance WITHOUT changing application code. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
questions.explanation: Read Replicas offload reads and need no app changes if handled at the connection layer. ElastiCache requires code to check the cache first, Multi-AZ is for HA (standby is not readable), and Aurora migration is more effort.

questions.question: A company wants S3 objects accessible ONLY through CloudFront and never directly via the S3 URL. What should they configure?
options: Set the S3 bucket ACL to private
questions.explanation: OAC restricts the S3 bucket so only the CloudFront service principal can read it (enforced via bucket policy). Signed URLs control who can access CloudFront content, not how CloudFront reaches S3.

questions.question: An application must remain available even if an entire Availability Zone fails. Which approach BEST meets this requirement?
options: Deploy a larger EC2 instance type
Deploy across multiple AZs behind an Elastic Load Balancer
Use an S3 Gateway VPC endpoint
questions.explanation: Spreading instances across multiple AZs behind an ELB provides fault tolerance: if one AZ fails, traffic routes to healthy instances in other AZs. Instance size alone does not add resilience.

questions.question: Objects in an S3 bucket are rarely accessed after 30 days but must be retrievable within milliseconds when needed. Which storage class is MOST cost-effective?
questions.explanation: S3 Standard-IA is for infrequently accessed data that still needs millisecond retrieval, at lower storage cost than Standard. Glacier has retrieval delays, and One Zone-IA sacrifices multi-AZ durability.

questions.question: A Lambda function's IAM role grants s3:GetObject, but calls fail with AccessDenied on a bucket whose bucket policy has an explicit Deny for all principals. Why?
options: The IAM role needs s3:ListBucket too
An explicit Deny always overrides any Allow
Lambda cannot access S3 without a VPC endpoint
The role trust policy is misconfigured
questions.explanation: In IAM policy evaluation, an explicit Deny always wins over any Allow. The bucket policy must be changed to remove the Deny or add an exception for the Lambda execution role ARN.

questions.question: Which Lambda invocation type is used when Amazon S3 triggers a function on object upload?
questions.explanation: S3 invokes Lambda asynchronously: the event is queued, Lambda retries twice on failure, and a Dead Letter Queue or destination can capture failures. API Gateway is synchronous; SQS/Kinesis/DynamoDB Streams are poll-based.

questions.question: A team wants to shift 10% of traffic to a new Lambda version, monitor it, then shift the rest. Which deployment approach does this describe?
questions.explanation: A canary deployment routes a small percentage (e.g., 10%) to the new version for a period, then shifts the remainder once it looks healthy. CodeDeploy supports canary and linear traffic shifting for Lambda aliases.

questions.question: A developer needs to store a database password securely with automatic rotation and native RDS integration. Which service is the BEST fit?
options: Environment variables in the Lambda function
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager provides built-in automatic rotation via Lambda and native integration with RDS/Redshift. Parameter Store Standard has no built-in rotation, and env vars/S3 are not purpose-built secret stores with rotation.

questions.question: An EC2 instance's memory usage is not visible in CloudWatch by default. How can you collect memory metrics?
options: Install and configure the CloudWatch agent
questions.explanation: Memory and disk usage are guest-OS metrics that EC2 does not publish by default. The CloudWatch agent (or legacy scripts) must be installed on the instance to push memory/disk metrics.

questions.question: You need SSH-like shell access to private EC2 instances with no open port 22, no bastion host, and full audit logging. Which service should you use?
options: EC2 Instance Connect over the internet
questions.explanation: SSM Session Manager provides shell access controlled by IAM, requires no inbound ports or bastion, and logs sessions to CloudWatch/S3, making it the most secure option.

questions.question: Which AWS service uses machine learning to continuously analyze VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail to detect threats like crypto-mining or credential compromise?
questions.explanation: GuardDuty is the managed threat-detection service that analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs. Macie classifies sensitive data in S3, Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, and Config tracks resource compliance.

questions.question: An organization wants to prevent any member account from disabling CloudTrail, regardless of that account's IAM permissions. What should be used?
options: A Service Control Policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations
An IAM identity policy on each user
questions.explanation: SCPs set the maximum available permissions for accounts in an OU/organization. A deny SCP on cloudtrail:StopLogging prevents even account admins from disabling CloudTrail. Permission boundaries and identity policies act only within a single account.

questions.question: A pipeline must fail and stop deployment if unit tests fail before packaging the artifact. Which service runs the build and tests in a CodePipeline stage?
questions.explanation: CodeBuild compiles code, runs tests, and produces artifacts; a failing test fails the build and halts the pipeline. CodeDeploy handles deployment, CodeCommit is source control, and CodeArtifact is a package repository.
